title: Lifecycle Environmental Sustainability & EU Heavy-Duty Fleet CO2 Mandates
description: Mastery-tier forensic and executive engineering module examining lifecycle environmental sustainability & eu heavy-duty fleet co2 mandates.
learning_objectives: Master professional Policy Argumentation & Counter-Claims in automotive engineering
Eliminate common Czech interference errors in lifecycle environmental sustainability & eu heavy-duty fleet co2 mandates
Demonstrate precision in technical and regulatory documentation

questions.prompt: The defense procurement tribunal mandated that the OEM _____ full finite element stress tensors for the armored chassis cab.

explanations.correct: Mastery-tier syntax: Mandative subjunctive requires base form 'furnish' after 'mandated that'.
explanations.wrong_A: Option 'furnishes' incorrectly applies indicative or non-inverted word order.
explanations.wrong_C: Option 'shall furnish' violates formal mandative subjunctive or inversion rules.
explanations.wrong_D: Option 'must to furnish' is ungrammatical in high-register technical legal discourse.

questions.cz_learning_point: High-level professional English prioritizes mandative subjunctive ('demand that it be done') and negative inversion ('Seldom have we seen') over colloquial indicative structures.

questions.prompt: It is imperative that every structural titanium alloy component _____ non-destructive Eddy current testing prior to military field trials.

explanations.correct: Mastery-tier syntax: Formulaic subjunctive after 'imperative that' requires base form 'undergo'.
explanations.wrong_A: Option 'undergoes' incorrectly applies indicative or non-inverted word order.
explanations.wrong_B: Option 'will undergo' violates formal mandative subjunctive or inversion rules.
explanations.wrong_D: Option 'must undergoes' is ungrammatical in high-register technical legal discourse.

explanations.wrong_C: Option 'did our metallurgists had' violates formal mandative subjunctive or inversion rules.
explanations.wrong_D: Option 'had our metallurgists have' is ungrammatical in high-register technical legal discourse.
